- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to adjust; apply lagged correction: if forecast > true, reduce by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is bullish; reduce forecast by 2–4% for first 7 days if sentiment >0.67.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to adjust forecast.
